A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V-OCBF study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, tables, and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original AGV and five MuJoCo simulation evaluations, controller comparisons, and network-size, disturbance, and expectile ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds boat-navigation comparisons, MuJoCo expectile experiments, and dynamics-model accuracy analyses.

M1.justification: Equations 9–10 and Algorithm 1 replace separate behavior-barrier training and explicit action-support gathering with direct expectile updates using a target bootstrapped from B_theta at the observed next state. Appendix A.3 also introduces a slack-penalized QP. These substantially revise the specified training and control procedures; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds boat navigation with state-dependent river drift, static obstacles, and bounded actuation. AGV collision avoidance and all five existing MuJoCo velocity-constrained tasks remain, making this a limited extension of domain coverage.

E2.justification: The new boat comparison in Table 9 evaluates CPQ, WSAC, CDT, and C2IQL alongside several retained competitors. These four additional methods substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set; the original AGV and MuJoCo comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols sweep four expectile values on three MuJoCo tasks and evaluate dynamics models trained for 50% and 25% of the standard budget, measuring prediction error on sampled state-action pairs. Existing dataset sizes, architectures, rollout metrics, and main evaluation sample counts are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained AGV ablations, v2 adds learned-barrier geometry across six expectiles, reward/cost sensitivity to expectiles on MuJoCo, and direct dynamics-underfitting tests with measured prediction errors. These substantially strengthen analysis of the central learning mechanism and sensitivity to model inaccuracies, previously investigated mainly through action noise.

E5.justification: Existing five-seed evaluations, reported uncertainties, standard-error description, and rollout percentile bands are retained. The boat comparison follows the existing five-seed practice; no new uncertainty estimator, significance test, or increased repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: Existing main results and Tables 1–6 are unchanged, but substantial new findings appear. Table 7 favors tau=0.9 over 0.99 on three MuJoCo tasks; Table 8 reports 96.32% safety with quarter-trained dynamics; Table 9 reports boat safety of 97.56±0.13% versus 88.43±0.59% for the strongest listed baseline, BC+NCBF. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical target/loss definitions in Equations 9–10 are revised, and Equation 22 introduces a formally specified relaxed QP. The finite-difference lemma and proof and the expectile definitions in Appendices A.1–A.2 are retained; no new learned-controller certification theorem is supplied.

C1.justification: v1 presents the framework as learning formally safe, safety-certified controllers. v2 restricts the invariance guarantee to an idealized setting without approximation errors and explicitly states that the learned barrier is not formally verified. This materially narrows the central safety claim while retaining the offline-learning and empirical-performance contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains how function approximation, finite data, and learned dynamics can invalidate closed-loop guarantees, and discusses relaxing safety constraints for QP feasibility. It also qualifies v1's favorable interpretation of tau approaching one: optimistic stochastic outcomes can make extreme expectiles brittle, with the new MuJoCo evidence supporting tau=0.9.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies tau=0.9 for main experiments, documents the boat dynamics and constraints, and names implementation sources for the additional baselines. Conversely, Table 11 removes v1 Table 8's shared Adam, learning-rate 10^-3, and ReLU specification. Existing hardware and architecture details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for WSAC, C2IQL, and conformal-prediction-based verification. Section 2.3 refines positioning around offline policy learning and using learned dynamics only during inference. The broader related-work survey remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, positioning, methodology, and limitations, plus new appendix subsections and a boat appendix that shifts Experimental Details from D to E. Affiliations and publication information change, but most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the six-panel expectile visualization and Tables 7–9. The environment illustration moves from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 5, while existing plots and tables are retained and reflowed. Publication headers and the shortened Algorithm 1 alter presentation without a comprehensive redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a central credibility problem: v1's formally safe-controller framing becomes an explicit distinction between idealized invariance and empirical safety of an unverified learned controller. The revised training specification and targeted expectile and model-fidelity experiments substantially improve assessment of the method's behavior and limitations. Additional boat comparisons strengthen empirical support. Missing slack-penalty settings and removed baseline optimization details leave reproducibility gaps, but these do not outweigh the substantial gains in claim accuracy and validation.
